rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.read: PPI came back hotter than the consensus (+1.3% m/m — biggest since March 2022; core +0.7%) and the market still faded the October hike: LSEG ~29% (from ~31.6% this morning, ~49% post-CPI); the 10-year fell ~27bp off Wednesday's 5.33% spike to ~5.05-5.10% (three-week low). MarketWatch: the hot print is 'still not turning market in favor of an October rate hike.' December ~90%+ untouched. Warsh speaks 10:30pm CT — the last voice before Saturday's blackout.

rows.title: Growth differentials
rows.read: Split surveys: Empire State +25.5 (big beat, new orders 23.2) vs Philly Fed 20.9 (miss, down from 37.8). Retail sales beat (+0.8%) but gasoline did the work — the control group ran just +0.1% vs 0.3% expected; claims 199K inline. Abroad: UK GDP beat +0.1% (3m/3m +0.7%); Australia jobs -39.3K with unemployment at a five-year high of 4.7%; Japan IP revised deeper to -2.4% against the +5.2% machinery-orders beat.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: Two hot wholesale prints in two days and the market looked through both: PPI +1.3% m/m (vs 0.6% expected; y/y 6.3% vs 5.5%), energy +10.8% m/m with gasoline +20.3% doing roughly half the headline's work, core +0.7% (vs 0.3%), core y/y 5.0%. What matters is what the bank does about it — October fading to ~29% says the Fed wants the calendar (midterms), not more data. France's final CPI confirmed the energy overshoot (HICP 3.4%, highest since Jan 2024); Swiss PPI missed (+0.3% vs 0.6%).

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.read: The AI risk-off deepened: Nasdaq -1.05% (fourth straight down day), the semiconductor index down an eighth straight session, CoreWeave bonds above 16%, VIX at a two-week high — and a defensive rotation (healthcare +2.6%, consumer staples +1%). The haven ladder: gold +1.8% ($4,181 futures), CHF +0.59%, JPY +0.34% — the franc out-bid the yen. Crypto offered no haven (BTC -2.4%, ~$1B in liquidations).

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities
rows.read: The EIA confirmed the draw (-8.6M vs +0.2M expected; 3% below the five-year average): December WTI +2.7% to $96.42 while December Brent sat ~$106.10 little changed — the spread compressed to ~$9.7 from ~$10.5. Shadow-fleet sanctions-easing talk leaked Brent's freight premium (Flynn: easing would be 'more negative for Brent than WTI'). Fresh US sanctions on Iran (16 individuals, 10 entities) kept the escalatory lane open. Gold ~$4,150-4,175 (+1.5%+) as the rate leg collapsed.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Unchanged intraday — COT is weekly (verified Oct 6 cut): DXY net long only +12,011 — modest, not crowded. The crowd is in EUR/AUD/GBP shorts (-99,332 / -98,588 / -97,611; EUR ~1st and AUD ~2nd percentile) — squeeze-loaded against any dovish surprise. Contrarian rule unchanged: stretched longs = unwind risk, stretched shorts = squeeze potential. Next COT Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.read: The EU summit's second day wrapped with no cohesion headline surfacing — the €100B+ war-driven fossil import bill stands as the euro's winter drag. France: the Oct 20 revenue-section vote and Moody's Oct 23 are the next gates; the 236-149 rejection failure holds. US: September's federal budget balance lands Friday; no new US fiscal development.
